title: Out-of-Order Multi-Copy Atomicity Assumption
pattern: Assuming that when a CPU updates a variable, all other CPUs in the system see that update at the exact same instant (multi-copy atomicity).
why_bad: On non-multicopy-atomic architectures (such as older ARM or POWER systems), CPU 1 can see CPU 0's write to `x` via a shared local cache and pass a signal via `y` to CPU 2, before the write to `x` has propagated over the global bus to CPU 2. CPU 2 will read `y == 1` but `x == 0`.
detection: Relying on multi-variable state assertions across 3+ threads without full memory barriers (`smp_mb()`) or sequentially consistent (`SeqCst`) atomics.
counterexample: Using `std::memory_order_seq_cst` or explicit full barriers on all read/write paths.
